messages:
saira: FYI saw a regional spike in eu-west-1 around 15:03 — a bunch of SDK clients started getting 429s but the payloads didn't include Retry-After. unclear client behavior is jammying our queues

tyler: yeah saw that too from the telemetry. backlog hit ~2.1x expected and our admission controller started returning soft-deny 429s without a clear hint header
	alex: are these hard 429s or soft admission denials? difference matters for client retry strategy
	emily: soft-admit. admission controller currently returns 429 + X-RW-Admit header with a float [0..1] and a window. but some older SDKs ignore it and do aggressive retries
	saira: example response we saw in logs:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Admit: 0.42; window=60
X-RW-Region: eu-west-1
X-RW-Queue-LagMs: 420
X-RW-Server-Id: pool-eu-3
{"error":"admission_denied","reason":"pool_saturation"}
```

jon: couple asks — (1) can the header format be standardized (single token or structured) so SDK parsers are tiny? (2) can we add a small suggested backoff param like `retry-ms`?
	tyl er: +1 to standardized. prefer a compact structured header like `X-RW-Admit: admit=0.42;window=60;retry_ms=300` so SDKs can compute pacing deterministically
	emily: we intentionally left `retry-ms` out because we want client-side jitter and adaptive pacing. but a hint value is reasonable as a soft suggestion (not authoritative).
	alex: for SDK guidance I'd recommend: if X-RW-Admit present then scale client concurrency by admit (ceil(max_concurrency*admit)), and apply capped exponential backoff with full-jitter starting at hint `retry_ms` when present
	saira: example pseudocode suggestion for SDK teams:

```
if header contains X-RW-Admit:
  target_concurrency = max(1, floor(cfg.max_concurrency * admit))
  wait_ms = header.retry_ms or 200
  backoff = min(10000, wait_ms * 2**retries)
  sleep(random_between(0, backoff))
else if 429 with Retry-After:
  sleep(parse_retry_after())
else:
  apply default capped backoff with jitter
```

jon: also two operational asks: (A) add X-RW-Queue-LagMs (we already do) and make it present for soft denies, (B) tag region/pool id so clients can fallback to multi-region configs instead of hammering the same pool
	op s-bot: incident-note: eu-west-1 GPU pool underprovisioned due to a provisioning job delay. mitigation: scaled new instances at 15:10, normalized at 15:23. Postmortem assigned to @saira.
	yler: other thing — network blips made some SDKs retry without honoring admit header; we should publish a small compatibility spec and ship a patch to go/python SDKs with builtin admit parser
	emily: Agreed. I'll draft a short SDK PR template and a one-page 'soft-429 semantics' doc: how to interpret admit, queue_lag, region, and fallback strategy. include recommended backoff numbers and a sample histogram cutoff for when to switch to geo-fallback
	alex: cost note: if clients immediately geo-fallback to higher-cost regions we could increase cross-region traffic and spend. SDKs should prefer scaling down concurrency first, then geo-fallback as a last resort (and honor admin-configured cost-awareness flags)
	saira: action items:
- emily to draft spec + SDK PR template (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- tyler + alex to propose header grammar and register in infra-api repo (ETA 48h)
- ops to add `retry_ms` as optional hint field and ensure region/pool present in soft-deny responses (ops: please coordinate)
	emily: will do. I'll include a short example response and client pseudo code in the doc
	jon: one more: can we emit a metric `client_hints_ignored` when a client retries more than N times within window despite admit < 0.5? would help measure adoption
	saira: good ask — ops/telemetry team can add that. I'll file ticket after this thread
	emily: thanks all, will loop in SDK owners in #devex when draft is ready :thumbsup:
